activities.anchor: One calibrated star type, one revolution
activities.caption: bet first — settling the island universes
activities.name: gxCepheidPredict

config.q: How did Hubble settle the Shapley–Curtis debate about the spiral nebulae?
choices: Cepheid variables in Andromeda — their period reveals true brightness, so their apparent dimness measures distance
A simply bigger telescope showed the nebulae were gas after all
The debate's judges voted on the better argument
config.why: Andromeda's Cepheids placed it ~900,000 light-years away (modern: 2.5 million) — far outside even the largest Milky Way estimate. Measurement outran philosophy.

activities.caption: file the census — which type does each trait describe?
activities.name: gxTypesBuckets

config.prompt: Hubble's tuning fork still organises the census:

items.label: smooth swarms of old, red, low-mass stars with little gas
discs, spiral arms, gas and ongoing star formation
the end products of mergers at cluster centres
gas-rich, shapeless dwarfs, often tidally mangled
the Milky Way — a barred member of the class

config.why: The types are histories, not species: what predicts a type is collision history, not age alone.

activities.anchor: galaxies grew their engines early and mostly switched off
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the galaxy's engine
activities.name: gxAGNCloze

config.text: An active galactic nucleus is a %%0%% black hole accreting matter at about %%1%% per cent efficiency — several times better than fusion — outshining the host's hundred billion stars from a region light-days across.
config.hint: Quasars cluster at redshift ~2 — engines grown early, mostly switched off.

activities.anchor: reading fossils in star orbits and metal abundances
activities.caption: rebuild the ecosystem loop
activities.name: gxEcoOrder

config.prompt: A galaxy in balance — put the loop in order:
items: Stellar winds and supernovae blow gas back out
The central black hole's AGN phase heats what remains
Star formation peaked at cosmic noon and has declined as reservoirs deplete
config.why: The universe formed most of its stars early and is slowly turning off — and galactic archaeology reads the eaten dwarfs in star orbits and metal abundances.

activities.anchor: no signal from beyond that horizon
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the observable radius
activities.name: gxRadiusEstimate

config.prompt: The universe is 13.8 billion years old, yet the observable universe's radius is far larger. Roughly how many billion light-years is that radius?
config.why: 46.5 billion light-years — expansion outran the light while it travelled, which is also why we receive no signal from beyond that horizon.
config.context: Running expansion backwards gives the Hubble time 1/H₀ ≈ 14 billion years, refined to 13.8 (Planck 2018).

activities.caption: pair each paradox with its resolution
activities.name: gxParadoxMatch

pairs.right: the stretching happens everywhere — every observer sees every other galaxy recede

pairs.left: a 46.5 Gly radius inside a 13.8 Gyr age
pairs.right: space expanded while the light travelled
every raisin sees the others move apart; none is the middle
an explosion in pre-existing space predicts a centre and an edge — we observe neither

config.why: The raisin-bread picture says otherwise: cosmological redshift is the stretching of space itself during the photon's journey.

activities.anchor: they checked the pigeon droppings first
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the three pillars' numbers
activities.name: gxCmbCloze

config.text: Big Bang nucleosynthesis predicts about %%0%% per cent hydrogen and %%1%% per cent helium by mass — and the oldest, most pristine gas clouds match. The cosmic microwave background, found as unremovable antenna noise, glows at %%2%% K.
config.hint: Penzias and Wilson, 1965 — the cooled afterglow of a hot dense beginning, 380,000 years in.
